1000137.etyen:
Borrowed from Italian (l')Eritrea, the name assigned to the Italian possessions on the Red Sea coast when they were constituted as the colony of Eritrea on 1 January 1890. Italian Eritrea was originally an ellipsis of Colonia eritrea (“Erythraean colony”), with eritrea the feminine form of eritreo (“Erythraean; of the Erythraean Sea”).
The Italian adjective is from Latin erythraeus (“reddish; Erythraean”), ultimately from Ancient Greek ἐρυθρός (eruthrós, “red”), from Proto-Hellenic *erutʰrós (“red”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rudʰrós (“red”), from the root *h₁rewdʰ- (“red, ruddy”). The name

1000393.etyen:

1005001.etyen:
PIE word
 *h₂m̥bʰi
Borrowed from French ambassadrice (“ambassador's wife; female ambassador”), the feminine counterpart of ambassadeur (“ambassador”) and related to ambassade (“embassy”). The wider word family ultimately goes back to Proto-Germanic *ambahtaz (“servant”), borrowed from Transalpine Gaulish ambaxtos (“vassal, high-ranking servant”), from Proto-Celtic *ambaxtos (“servant”), formed from *ambi- (“around”) and *ageti (“to drive”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂m̥bʰi (“around”) and *h₂eǵ- (“to drive”).
Compare the related embete (“office, post”), as well as Danish ambassadric
